message.content: Pandas belong to the family Ursidae (bears). Their lineage diverged from other bears around 20–25 million years ago. Fossil evidence shows that early giant panda ancestors were omnivorous, but over time they adapted to a bamboo-dominated diet. By the Pleistocene, the modern giant panda had evolved its distinctive black-and-white coat and specialized wrist bone that acts like a thumb for grasping bamboo. The red panda, though sharing the name, belongs to its own family Ailuridae and diverged earlier, around 40–50 million years ago.
